test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Nagaland was declared as a separate state on _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st December 1963**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nagaland was officially declared the 16th state of India on **1st December 1963**.
 
• It was formed after the enactment of the State of Nagaland Act, 1962.
 
• Nagaland consists of 11 districts with Kohima being its capital.
 
• The state was created to recognize the unique culture and identity of the Naga people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State of Nagaland Act, 1962:**

 
 
• This Act was passed by the Indian Parliament to provide for the formation of the state of Nagaland.
 
• It outlined the territorial extent, the composition of the legislative assembly, and other administrative details.
 
 
 
• **Formation of States in India:**
 
 
• India has undergone several reorganizations of states since its independence in 1947.
 
• The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 was a major reform that reorganized the boundaries of India's states based on linguistic lines.
 
• New states have since been created to address various demands for autonomy and recognition of cultural identities.
 
 
 
• **Naga People:**
 
 
• The Nagas are an indigenous ethnic group native to the northeastern part of India and northwestern Myanmar.
 
• They have a rich cultural heritage, including traditional dances, music, and festivals such as the Hornbill Festival.
 
• The demand for a separate state by the Naga people was driven by their desire to preserve their distinct cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nagaland's Statehood:**
 
 
• The creation of Nagaland as a state helped to address the political and cultural aspirations of the Naga people.
 
• It provided a framework for self-governance and development within the Indian Union.
 
• Nagaland's statehood has contributed to the preservation and promotion of Naga culture and traditions.
